'''César Sánchez Domínguez''' ({{IPA|es|ˈθesaɾ ˈsantʃeθ}}; born 2 September 1971), sometimes known as simply '''César''', is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]].

He played 401 [[La Liga]] games in 20 seasons, with [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]], [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]], [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] and [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], being first choice in three of those clubs and winning six major titles with the second, including the [[2002 UEFA Champions League final|2002 Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.com/noticias/momento-historico-cesar-sanchez|title=Momento histórico: César Sánchez|trans-title=Historic moment: César Sánchez|publisher=[[La Liga]]|language=Spanish|date=3 September 2021|accessdate=24 July 2025}}</ref> He also appeared once for [[Spain national football team|Spain]].

From January to June 2020, César was [[sporting director]] at Valencia.

==Club career==
===Valladolid and Real Madrid===
César was born in [[Coria, Cáceres]], [[Extremadura]]. He graduated from [[Real Valladolid]]'s youth academy, and made his debut with the first team in a 0–6 home defeat against [[FC Barcelona]] where he [[Substitute (association football)|came on]] for [[Mauro Ravnić]] early into the second half, at the end of the [[1991–92 La Liga|1991–92 season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca-paginas.mundodeportivo.com/EMD01/HEM/1992/05/25/MD19920525-002.pdf|title=Goleada de miedo|trans-title=Scary rout|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=Joan|last=Domènech|language=Spanish|date=25 May 1992|accessdate=8 April 2016}}</ref> He only missed a total of four league games between 1995 and 2000.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vavel.com/es/futbol/real-valladolid/241086-corregir-modificar-segundo-parrafo-pucelano-historico-cesar-sanchez.html|title=Pucelano histórico: César Sánchez|trans-title=Historic ''pucelano'': César Sánchez|publisher=Vavel|first=Alvar|last=Salvador|language=Spanish|date=1 June 2013|accessdate=8 April 2016}}</ref>

Sánchez signed ahead of [[2000–01 La Liga|2000–01]] for [[La Liga]] giants [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], initially backing up wonderkid [[Iker Casillas]]. However, the [[2001–02 La Liga|following campaign]], he eventually became first-choice and started five out of nine [[UEFA Champions League]] matches during the [[Madrid|capital]] side's [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League|victorious run]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.abc.es/realmadrid/noticias/20150715/abci-porteros-madrid-casillas-201507081647.html|title=Casillas, 12 compañeros en la portería en sus 16 años en el primer equipo|trans-title=Casillas, 12 goal teammates in his 16 years in the first team|newspaper=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|first=Raúl|last=Martín|language=Spanish|date=15 July 2015|accessdate=24 July 2025}}</ref> but was [[Substitute (association football)|substituted]] by Casillas in [[2002 UEFA Champions League final|the final]] with [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen]] after suffering an injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/UCL/News/Kind=128/newsId=23850.html|title=Madrid win ninth European crown|publisher=UEFA|date=15 May 2002|accessdate=8 April 2016|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20020606223553/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/UCL/News/Kind%3D128/newsId%3D23850.html|archivedate=6 June 2002}}</ref>

===Zaragoza and Tottenham===
César joined [[Real Zaragoza]] for [[2005–06 La Liga|2005–06]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news/01aa-0e6ce764c530-3abb56c534ee-1000--cesar-switches-to-zaragoza/|title=César switches to Zaragoza|publisher=UEFA|date=13 June 2005|accessdate=22 March 2025}}</ref> and was everpresent in the [[Aragon]]ese side's lineups during three seasons. In August 2008, after their relegation to [[Segunda División]], new manager [[Marcelino García Toral]] sent the player to [[Real Zaragoza B|the reserves]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archivo.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/2a_division/zaragoza/es/desarrollo/1154185.html|title=Juande 'rescata' a César y se lo lleva al Tottenham|trans-title=Juande 'rescues' César and takes him to Tottenham|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|first=Sonia|last=Gaudioso|language=Spanish|date=8 August 2008|accessdate=8 April 2016}}</ref>

Shortly after, Sánchez was bought by [[Juande Ramos]]'s [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/articles/sanchezsigns120808.html|title=Sánchez signs|publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C|date=12 August 2008|accessdate=19 August 2008}}</ref> He made his only appearance for the London club in a 4–2 victory over [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in the [[2008–09 Football League Cup|fourth round]] of the [[EFL Cup|Football League Cup]], replacing the injured [[Heurelho Gomes]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/league_cup/7708820.stm|title=Tottenham 4–2 Liverpool|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|first=Sam|last=Lyon|date=11 November 2008|accessdate=12 November 2008}}</ref>

===Valencia===
César returned to Spain on 20 January 2009, joining [[Valencia CF]] on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]] until the end of [[2008–09 La Liga|the season]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.levante-emv.com/secciones/noticia.jsp?pRef=2009012100_11_545351__Deportes-Cesar-elegido|title=César es el elegido|trans-title=César is the chosen one|newspaper=[[Levante-EMV]]|first=Amparo|last=Barbeta|language=Spanish|date=21 January 2009|accessdate=21 January 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120318101656/http://www.levante-emv.com/secciones/noticia.jsp?pRef=2009012100_11_545351__Deportes-Cesar-elegido|archive-date=18 March 2012}}</ref> as the ''Che'' had just lost first-choice [[Renan (footballer, born January 1985)|Renan]] to a groin injury, during a 3–2 loss at [[Athletic Bilbao]]. Despite this, the former was still named on the bench for a Tottenham game on the 21st, the League Cup semi-final second leg against [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]];<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/league_cup/7824257.stm|title=Burnley 3–2 Tottenham (agg 4–6)|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Ian|last=Hughes|date=21 January 2009|accessdate=28 March 2020}}</ref> two days later, Tottenham announced that his contract had been cancelled by mutual consent,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/articles/sanchezdeparts230109.html|title=Sanchez departs|publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C|date=23 January 2009|accessdate=23 January 2009}}</ref> and he retained his starting status even when the Brazilian recovered from his injury.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2009/06/12/mas_futbol/1244788025_850215.html|title=Le buscan cesión a Renan y César aún puede renovar|trans-title=Loan wanted for Renan and César may still renew|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|first=M.A.|last=Vara|language=Spanish|date=12 June 2009|accessdate=8 April 2016}}</ref>

After an impressive half-season, César renewed his contract for another year.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2009/06/24/futbol/equipos/valencia/1245866573.html|title=César renueva con el Valencia|trans-title=César renews with Valencia|newspaper=Marca|language=Spanish|date=24 June 2009|accessdate=25 June 2009}}</ref> He started the [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10 campaign]] on the bench, playing second-fiddle to new signing [[Miguel Ángel Moyá]]; however, after unconvincing displays by the latter, he regained the starting spot,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.superdeporte.es/valencia/2010/02/17/portero-deberia-jugar-brujas-moya-o-cesar/87244.html|title=¿Qué portero debería jugar contra el Brujas, Moyà o César?|trans-title=What goalkeeper should play against Brugge, Moyà or César?|newspaper=[[Super Deporte]]|first=J. E.|last=Carratalá|language=Spanish|date=17 February 2010|accessdate=8 April 2016}}</ref> keeping consecutive [[Shutout#Association football|clean sheets]] against [[Racing de Santander]] (1–0),<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2009_10/primera/jornada_6/rac_val/|title=Pinillos se confundió con Zigic|trans-title=Pinillos thought he was Zigic|newspaper=Marca|first=Fran|last=Villalobos|language=Spanish|date=4 October 2009|accessdate=8 April 2016}}</ref> defending champions Barcelona (0–0),<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2009_10/primera/jornada_7/val_bar/|title=El Valencia frena al líder|trans-title=Valencia halt leaders|newspaper=Marca|first=Ramiro|last=Aldunate|language=Spanish|date=18 October 2009|accessdate=8 April 2016}}</ref> [[UD Almería]] (3–0)<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.publico.es/actualidad/valencia-quita-presion-visita-almeria.html|title=0–3. El Valencia se quita la presión en su visita a Almería|trans-title=0–3. Valencia shake pressure off in visit to Almería|newspaper=[[Público (Spain)|Público]]|language=Spanish|date=25 October 2009|accessdate=8 April 2016}}</ref> and [[Málaga CF]] (1–0).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spanish-football/2009/11/01/1597998/malaga-0-1-valencia-navarro-wins-it-for-los-che|title=Malaga 0–1 Valencia: Navarro wins it for Los Che|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|first=Paul|last=Madden|date=1 November 2009|accessdate=8 April 2016}}</ref> In May 2010, after helping Valencia to third place, with the team consequently [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League|returning to the Champions League]], the veteran agreed to a further one-year extension.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/es/news/21/fichajes/2010/05/20/1934719/mercado-el-valencia-renueva-al-veterano-portero-c%C3%A9sar|title=Mercado: El Valencia renueva al veterano portero César|trans-title=Market: Valencia renew veteran goalkeeper César|publisher=Goal|language=Spanish|date=20 May 2010|accessdate=8 April 2016}}</ref>

On 2 April 2011, César became the second oldest goalkeeper in Spanish League history as he appeared – as a starter – in a 4–2 defeat of [[Getafe CF]], aged 39 years and 212 days.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.superdeporte.es/valencia/2011/04/02/cesar-portero-veterano-liga/124065.html|title=César, el portero más veterano de la Liga|trans-title=César, the League's most veteran goalkeeper|newspaper=Super Deporte|language=Spanish|date=2 April 2011|accessdate=6 June 2011}}</ref> He contributed 15 appearances, as his team [[2010–11 La Liga|finished third]] and [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League|qualified for the Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/01f1-0e788ae3eb6c-978df7c1bff1-1000--valencia-s-emery-aims-high-after-new-one-year-deal/|title=Valencia's Emery aims high after new one-year deal|publisher=UEFA|date=23 May 2011|accessdate=24 July 2025}}</ref>

===Later career===
However, after the club acquired [[Diego Alves]] and renewed youth graduate [[Vicente Guaita]]'s contract, César became surplus to requirements. On 2 June 2011, he signed a one-year deal with [[Valencian Community]] neighbours [[Villarreal CF]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2011/06/02/2514935/cesar-sanchez-joins-villarreal-report|title=Cesar Sanchez joins Villarreal – report|publisher=Goal|date=2 June 2011|accessdate=4 June 2011}}</ref> making his league debut on 10 September in a 2–2 home draw against [[Sevilla FC]]: after replacing [[Ejection (sports)|sent off]] [[Diego López (Spanish footballer, born 1981)|Diego López]] early into the first half, he stopped the ensuing [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] by [[Álvaro Negredo]], whom however managed to score with a putback.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/324010?cc=5739|title=Villarreal claim battling draw|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=10 September 2011|accessdate=12 September 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102085423/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/324010?cc=5739|archive-date=2 November 2012}}</ref> Subsequently, he became only the fifth player to appear in a Spanish top division match over the age of 40, following [[Harry Lowe (footballer, born August 1886)|Harry Lowe]], [[Jacques Songo'o]], [[Amedeo Carboni]] and [[Donato (footballer)|Donato]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://espndeportes.espn.com/futbol/cronica?id=151473|title=Última alegría para el Deportivo|trans-title=Last joy for Deportivo|publisher=[[ESPN Deportes]]|language=Spanish|date=21 May 2004|accessdate=21 February 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2017/12/28/album/1514471476_986533.html|title=Los futbolistas con más edad que han jugado en LaLiga|trans-title=Oldest footballers to have played in LaLiga|newspaper=Diario AS|language=Spanish|date=28 December 2017|accessdate=28 March 2020}}</ref>

César returned to the [[Mestalla Stadium]] on 20 January 2020, being appointed [[sporting director]] on a two-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/deportes/futbol/2020/01/20/5e25951421efa0ef1c8b459b.html|title=El Valencia ficha a César Sánchez como director de fútbol|trans-title=Valencia sign César Sánchez as director of football|newspaper=El Mundo|first=Inma|last=Lidón|language=Spanish|date=20 January 2020|accessdate=28 March 2020}}</ref> However, five months later, he resigned from the post.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eldesmarque.com/valencia/valencia-cf/252847-el-mensaje-de-despedida-de-cesar-sanchez-vestido-de-corto|title=El mensaje de despedida de César Sánchez vestido de corto|trans-title=César Sánchez's farewell message in uniform|publisher=El Desmarque|first=David|last=Torres|language=Spanish|date=29 June 2020|accessdate=21 September 2020}}</ref>

==International career==
César earned his only [[Cap (sport)|cap]] for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] on 16 August 2000, in a 4–1 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] defeat to [[Germany national football team|Germany]] in [[Hannover]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/2000/08/17/pagina-10/684495/pdf.html|title=Desastre|trans-title=Disaster|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Javier|last=Gascón|language=Spanish|date=17 August 2000|accessdate=6 June 2014}}</ref>
